title: Rewind to video, and two pointers on moving pieces
blurb: The history kept by <dom-rewind> is encoded to a video file with WebCodecs, and eight moving pieces of HTML are pressed with two fingers at once to see which piece the browser sends each pointer to.
question: Can the recorded past of live HTML be encoded as video, and can two pointers at once each reach the moving piece under them?
result: Yes to the first: frames() gives bitmaps that a VideoEncoder accepts, and the WebM plays. For the second, one element has one hit box, so only one pointer is right. One element for each piece, or a canvas that routes each pointer itself, makes both right.

openSnapshots.why: known: experiment 1 is a rewind buffer of ElementImage snapshots (lib/dom-rewind.js). It keeps one per changed element per frame for 12 seconds and closes them as they leave the buffer.
